title: Strategy Advisor (I) (LtCol to Maj) FMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
5.     MOS 0508, Strategy Advisor (I) (LtCol to Maj) FMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Strategy Advisors are educated in the reciprocity of war
and strategy, warfighting, and strategic interagency/coalition decision-
making. They provide a complex level of analyses to assist senior leader
decision making. Strategy Advisors represent the Marine Corps at the
combatant command, joint staff, Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD)
levels and higher. 0508 billets are listed as additional skills designators



                                          1-32                        Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



and maintained by DC PP&O and DC M&RA to ensure appropriate billets are
staffed with Strategy Advisors.

    b. Prerequisites. Selection by the top-level school board to a program
that offers advanced strategy courses as defined by DC PP&O and MCU.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete one of the following Top Level School Advanced Strategy
Courses (TLS-ASC):

                (a) Naval War College, Advanced Strategist Program.

                (b) Army War College, Advanced Strategic Art Program.

            (c) Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies
Strategic Thinkers Program.

            (d) School of Advanced Military Studies, Advanced Strategic
Leadership Studies Program.

            (e) Air War College, Air Force Grand Strategy Seminar or Air
Force Joint Warfighter Studies Seminar.

        (2) DC PP&O is the adjudication authority for Top Level School
programs that result in this FMOS being awarded.

        (3) This MOS will be assigned to a Marine in an appropriate service,
joint, or OSD planning billet by submitting a graduation certificate through
the Marine’s servicing IPAC.

    d. Duties. Strategy Advisors assist senior leader decision making to
address complex problems through rigorous systemic thinking. They
contextualize problems sets through lenses of past, current, and proposed
strategies, wars, and eras of competition into their larger contexts. This
analysis allows Strategy Advisors to delve into a problem set’s myriad
dimensions and offer detailed analyses.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
